summary: Grace Hill's August 2026 packaging strategy (prepared by Revenue Management Labs) starts from the observation that no single buyer naturally owns the full Grace Hill portfolio, which creates fragmented budgets and decision rights across L&D/HR, Marketing, Asset Management/BD and Operations. The response is a three-decision purchase structure: first choose a platform tier (PHQ Platform Core or PHQ Platform Plus), then choose one or both solution tracks (Track 1 Workforce Excellence for L&D/Ops, Track 2 Resident & Prospect Satisfaction for Marketing), then add à la carte add-ons that sit outside the tiers. An earlier Friday recommendation carried a third track, Market Advantage for Asset Mgmt/BD; in the revised structure HelloData was rolled up into the platform layer instead (HelloData Lite in Core, HelloData Complete in Plus), while remaining available as a standalone solution for 'HelloData purists' who explicitly do not want to adopt PHQ. Everything is priced per unit per month (additional mystery shops per shop), so cost scales with the portfolio rather than seat count. Because the track structure fits different buyers with different budgets and a combined sale has a long cycle, the go-to-market motion is to lead with one track and expand into others and add-ons — expansion is a tier upgrade, not new scope.

packages.name: PHQ Platform Core
packages.positioning: The base platform layer — the connected picture. Decision 1 of 3: choose your platform.
packages.buyer: Required with any track; the exec sponsor above both functional buyers is needed for a full-platform buy.
packages.whenToLead: Broadest land is a full-platform entry at Core where the buyer wants both tracks live from day one on the base data layer — one platform of record across workforce, resident and prospect signals. Also the default entry for functional-buyer deals: lead with Core and show Plus at renewal.
packages.notes: Priced per unit per month. Expansion from Core to Plus is a tier upgrade, not new scope.

packages.name: PHQ Platform Plus
packages.positioning: The upgrade tier — adds AI action plans, open data access and full market data on top of Core.
includes: Data Integration through exposed APIs and MCP connector for AI assistants
packages.buyer: Buyers who own portfolio-level P&L accountability; enterprise buyers standardizing on the platform.
packages.whenToLead: Sell where the buyer needs full comp and market data to benchmark results against comps (HelloData Complete is the differentiator), where the buyer owns portfolio-level P&L accountability, or in reputation-recovery deals needing market benchmarking against comps. Plus across the platform and both tracks is the enterprise-standard scenario — highest ACV, longest cycle.
packages.notes: Priced per unit per month. In the earlier Friday recommendation this tier was named 'PHQ Platform Advanced'; the revised structure names it Plus and moves HelloData into the platform layer.

packages.name: Track 1 — Workforce Excellence
packages.positioning: Develop people and drive operational consistency. Decision 2 of 3: choose your track(s).
includes: Core: Essential role-specific content + engaging learning formats
Core: Instructor-led and virtual classroom training
Plus adds: Additional role-specific content + custom courses
Plus adds: Combo mystery shops (2 / Property / Year)
Plus adds: Skill-gap insights and micro-learning courses
packages.buyer: L&D / Ops (budget owner: L&D, HR, Operations). Primary need: workforce capability and compliance to support consistent property operations and employee development.
packages.whenToLead: Compliance-driven entry — L&D/Ops needs mandated training (fair housing, safety, harassment) to close an audit or insurance gap. This is the fastest cycle and highest volume; lead with Core and show Plus at renewal. Performance-driven entry — a buyer chasing on-site execution who wants Mystery Shopping and Employee Surveys from day one; larger operator, longer cycle, with mystery shops and employee surveys acting as the wedge.
packages.notes: Available at Core or Plus. Underlying solutions: Training, Policies, Mystery Shopping, Employee Surveys.

packages.name: Track 2 — Resident & Prospect Satisfaction
packages.positioning: Improve the resident and prospect experience. Decision 2 of 3: choose your track(s).
includes: Core: ORM — Reputation monitoring and response
Plus adds: ORM — Feedback and sentiment analysis (AI)
packages.buyer: Marketing (budget owner: Marketing, Operations). Primary need: resident and prospect experience to drive leasing performance, retention and reputation.
packages.whenToLead: Resident satisfaction entry — Marketing owns reputation scores and wants resident sentiment and survey data; a Marketing-led land with Track 2 Core as the wedge and Track 1 as the later cross-sell. Prospect conversion entry — buyer focused on tour-to-lease conversion who wants mystery shopping of the leasing funnel, where prospect-side shops are the differentiator. Reputation-recovery entry — a portfolio with weak review scores needing diagnostics plus a remediation plan; urgency-driven, pair with Platform Plus for market benchmarking against comps.
packages.notes: Available at Core or Plus. Underlying solutions: Resident & Prospect Surveys, Reputation Management, Realync.

packages.name: Track 3 — Market Advantage
packages.positioning: Competitive intelligence and benchmarking to support day-to-day operations as well as acquisitions. Proposed in the Friday packaging recommendation and NOT carried into the revised packaging structure — do not present as current.
includes: Plus adds: Portfolio & multi-market analysis / Financial Analysis (acquisition specific)
Plus adds: Rent-roll and underwriting insights
packages.buyer: Asset Mgmt / BD (budget owner: Asset Mgmt, BD, Operations).
packages.notes: Dropped in the revised structure. Feedback (pushbacks) was that every operational buyer needs comp data, so HelloData must span all tracks, and that HelloData purists resist being PHQ customers — so Market Advantage doesn't need its own track since HelloData-only buyers skip the other tracks. HelloData was rolled up into the platform layer (HelloData Lite in Core, HelloData Complete in Plus) while remaining available as a separate standalone solution for HelloData purists who explicitly do not want to adopt PHQ.

packages.name: Add-Ons (à la carte, outside the tiers)
packages.positioning: Decision 3 of 3: choose your add-ons. Sold outside the tier structure.
packages.whenToLead: Attach to a track deal rather than leading with them; used as expansion beyond the initial track.
packages.notes: Priced à la carte; additional mystery shops are charged per shop rather than per unit per month.

packages.name: HelloData standalone
packages.positioning: HelloData remains available as a separate standalone solution for 'HelloData purists' who explicitly do not want to adopt PHQ.
packages.buyer: HelloData-only buyers who skip the PHQ tracks.
packages.whenToLead: When the buyer explicitly does not want to adopt PerformanceHQ.
packages.notes: The source states this as a carve-out from the platform roll-up rather than describing its contents; no component list is given in the deck.

principles: No single buyer naturally owns the full Grace Hill portfolio, creating fragmented budgets and decision rights.
Buyer and budget ownership patterns imply the solution tracks — package around who holds the budget, not around the product catalog.
Three decisions, not a long menu: 1) choose your platform, 2) choose your track(s), 3) choose your add-ons.
Everything priced per unit per month (additional shops per shop), so cost scales with the portfolio rather than with a seat count.
The track structure fits different buyers with different budgets, which means a combined sales cycle is long — lead with one track and expand to others and add-ons.
Every operational buyer needs comp data, so HelloData must span all tracks — it sits in the platform layer (Lite in Core, Complete in Plus) rather than in its own track.
Market Advantage doesn't need its own track since HelloData-only buyers skip the other tracks.
Known risk to manage: packaging can feel 'siloed' — the cross-signal promise isn't visible unless buyers purchase multiple tracks.
Expansion is a tier upgrade, not new scope — say so plainly to the buyer.
A platform buy (both tracks) requires an exec sponsor above both functional buyers.
Lead with Core and show Plus at renewal on the fastest-cycle functional deals.

migrationNotes: The deck does not lay out a migration path for existing customers onto the new packaging. The only statements bearing on movement between packages are that expansion is a tier upgrade rather than new scope, that the recommended motion is to lead with one track and expand to other tracks and add-ons later, that Core buyers should be shown Plus at renewal, and that HelloData — although rolled up into the platform layer — remains available as a separate standalone solution for HelloData purists who explicitly do not want to adopt PerformanceHQ.
pricingNote: Internal pricing figures were deliberately excluded from this file. The source deck states only the pricing structure — everything priced per unit per month, with additional mystery shops charged per shop — which is retained here as positioning. No per-unit rates, discount ladders or floor prices are included.
